literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒研究取得多项新进展:机制、防控与监测并重。
literature.lead_zh: 近期多项研究揭示了诺如病毒感染机制、环境传播途径及新型防控技术,为公共卫生应对提供了新思路。
key_findings_zh: 人类诺如病毒感染不会在人类肠道类器官中诱导血清素分泌,这表明呕吐症状可能不直接由上皮细胞血清素释放引起 [10.1128/jvi.00833-26]。
多胺 depletion 可显著抑制小鼠和人类诺如病毒感染,为开发靶向宿主代谢的抗病毒策略提供了新靶点 [10.1128/mbio.02033-26]。
诺如病毒 GII.17[P17]在全球范围内自2023年以来再次流行,其主要谱系扩散中心已从东亚转移到西欧 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1861818]。
气溶胶化鼠源性诺如病毒在空气中保持感染性长达9小时,支持其通过空气传播的可能性 [10.1016/j.jhin.2026.09.023]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 诺如病毒正呈现全球性流行趋势,环境和空气传播途径增加了防控难度,亲和力较低的 GII.17[P17]正迅速扩散。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分研究使用动物模型或体外培养系统,结果可能无法完全代表人类感染情况;部分为数学建模或预印本研究,需谨慎解释。
literature.headline_en: Advances in Norovirus Research: Mechanisms, Prevention, and Surveillance Converge.
literature.lead_en: Recent studies reveal novel insights into norovirus infection mechanisms, environmental transmission routes, and emerging control technologies, offering new strategies for public health response.
key_findings_en: Human norovirus infection does not induce serotonin secretion in intestinal organoids, suggesting vomiting may not result from direct epithelial serotonin release [10.1128/jvi.00833-26]
Polyamine depletion significantly inhibits both murine and human norovirus infection, identifying polyamine metabolism as a promising host-targeting antiviral strategy [10.1128/mbio.02033-26]
Norovirus GII.17[P17] has resurged globally since 2023, with its primary lineage dispersal center shifting from East Asia to Northwest Europe [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1861818]
Aerosolized murine norovirus retains infectivity for up to 9 hours, supporting the plausibility of airborne transmission during outbreaks [10.1016/j.jhin.2026.09.023]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Norovirus is showing a global resurgence trend, with environmental and airborne transmission routes increasing control challenges, and the low-fitness GII.17[P17] lineage is spreading rapidly.
literature.caveats_en: Some studies use animal models or in vitro systems, which may not fully represent human infection; some are mathematical models or preprints and should be interpreted cautiously.
literature.brief_en: Recent research advances in norovirus span virology, transmission dynamics, and vaccine development. Studies highlight that norovirus does not directly trigger serotonin-mediated vomiting in organoids, that polyamine depletion blocks viral infection, and that GII.17[P17] is undergoing global expansion with shifted phylogeographic origins. Airborne transmission is also supported by aerosol stability data. These findings inform new therapeutic targets, surveillance strategies, and vaccine design approaches.

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 诺如病毒 暴发 导致英国一家医院关闭了两个病房以接收新患者,因为该医院正在管理多起该病毒病例。 [news-b5038b0bd4bf0d08]
暴发 的 诺如病毒 导致西岛医院的内科病房 2 和外科病房关闭,仅允许特定群体进行必要的探访。 [news-e5cc818d401aee22]
加尔各答至少3家医院已报告诺如病毒病例,症状严重,如脱水、呕吐、肠胃炎等。一些患者被送入 ICU,其他患者则在 OPD 接受治疗。 [news-612a4d12512290b8]
瑞典进行了诺如病毒调查,发现来自KwangCheonKim Co.的寿司海藻诺如病毒 GII检测呈阳性。不过,瑞典食品局并未得出海藻是食物中毒原因的结论。制造商KwangCheonKim Co.通过了食品药品安全部的认证,并对其制造过程进行了检查。 [news-663573add6284c89]
根据对患者样本的检测,专家证实,罗德岛大量胃肠炎病例是由于诺如病毒 暴发而不是受污染的水造成的。 [news-543d07c225a559e9]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: A norovirus outbreak has led to the closure of two wards at a UK hospital to new patients, as the hospital is managing several cases of the virus. [news-b5038b0bd4bf0d08]
An outbreak of norovirus has led to the closure of medical ward 2 and the surgical ward at Western Isles Hospital, with essential visiting only allowed for specific groups. [news-e5cc818d401aee22]

Norovirus cases have been reported in at least three hospitals in Kolkata, with severe symptoms such as dehydration, vomiting, and gastroenteritis. Some patients were admitted to the ICU, and others were treated at OPDs. [news-612a4d12512290b8]

Sweden conducted a norovirus probe and found that sushi seaweed from KwangCheonKim Co. tested positive for norovirus GII. However, the Swedish Food Agency did not conclude that the seaweed was the cause of the food poisoning. [news-663573add6284c89]
Experts confirmed that the high number of gastroenteritis cases on Rhodes is due to a norovirus outbreak, not contaminated water, based on tests of patient samples. [news-543d07c225a559e9]

papers.title: Global Diversity of Norovirus Genotypes from 2002 to 2025: A Review of Temporal, Age-Specific and Regional Trends
papers.abstract: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in young children and older adults. This study characterizes the global prevalence and diversity of norovirus genotypes among sporadic cases. A review of English-language studies (published 2002–2026) that characterized norovirus genotype distribution among sporadic cases was conducted, excluding outbreak and asymptomatic detections. Pooled data were analyzed with stratifications by age group, region, and year of sample collection. A total of 20,588 cases were identified from 72 publications. There were 30 genotypes identified, with GII.4, GII.3, GII.2, GII.17, and GII.6 and each accounting for ≥5% of detections. GII.4 was the predominant genotype globally, accounting for 54% of cases and up to 80% among older adults across all years, but periodic fluctuation was seen, coinciding with fluctuations in the prevalence of other genotypes, especially GII.3, GII.2, and GII.17. Among GI genotypes, GI.3 was most prevalent (46%), particularly among adults. Genotype diversity was highest among children in low- and middle-income countries and in Asia/Oceania. Findings indicate that a small number of genotypes account for most cases. As genotyping characterizes the major capsid protein, the primary target of antibody recognition, findings have important implications for vaccine development and public health interventions.

papers.abstract_zh: 诺如病毒是全球急性胃肠炎(急性胃肠炎)的主要病因,具有显著的发病率和死亡率,尤其是在儿童和老年人中。本研究描述了患病率(急性胃肠炎)的全球分布及诺如病毒基因型的多样性。对2002年至2026年发表的英文文献进行了综述,这些文献描述了诺如病毒基因型在散发病例中的分布情况,排除了暴发和无症状检测。通过按年龄组、地区和样本采集年份进行分层分析,对汇总数据进行了分析。从72篇文献中总共识别出20,588例病例。共鉴定出30种基因型,其中GII.4、GII.3、GII.2、GII.17和GII.6每种基因型的检测占比均≥5%。GII.4是全球主要的基因型,占病例总数的54%,在老年人中占比高达80%,但其流行趋势存在周期性波动,与其它基因型(尤其是GII.3、GII.2和GII.17)的波动相吻合。在GI基因型中,GI.3最为常见(46%),尤其是在成年人中。低收入和中等收入国家的儿童以及亚洲/大洋洲地区的基因型多样性最高。研究结果表明,少数几种基因型占大多数病例。由于基因型鉴定主要针对主要衣壳蛋白,而该蛋白是抗体识别的主要靶标,因此这些发现对疫苗(抗病毒药物)的研发和公共卫生干预具有重要意义。

papers.title: Polyamine depletion inhibits murine and human norovirus infection
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Noroviruses are non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA viruses in the family Caliciviridae. Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are the leading cause of viral gastrointestinal disease. Despite their clinical relevance, therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited, partly due to challenges in cultivating HNoV and limited understanding of virus-host interactions. Polyamines (PAs) are small polycationic metabolites derived from amino acid metabolism that are essential for diverse cellular functions and serve as important host factors for many RNA viruses. However, their role in norovirus infection has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate that PAs are critical for productive infection for both HNoV and murine norovirus (MNV), underscoring a conserved and functionally significant dependency across species. Functional analysis in MNV-infected cells showed that PA depletion resulted in a marked reduction in major capsid protein synthesis and reduced viral titers following the first replication cycle, coinciding with a loss of virus-induced cytopathic effect (CPE). In PA-depleted cells, viral titers and CPE could be restored by exogenous supplementation with spermine or spermidine (metabolites of the PA biosynthetic pathway), cholesterol, or a PI3-kinase inhibitor. In addition to MNV, depletion of PAs completely ablated HNoV infection in human intestinal enteroids, which was also partially rescued by adding exogenous PAs. Collectively, these findings identify PAs as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and highlight PA metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for antiviral intervention against HNoV. IMPORTANCE: Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide, yet the development of effective antivirals and vaccines has been hampered by the lack of small-animal models and robust in vitro systems to propagate the virus. Murine norovirus (MNV) shares key features with HNoV and serves as a valuable surrogate for studying norovirus biology. In this study, we identify host-derived polyamines (PAs) as essential and conserved metabolites required for productive infection for both HNoV and MNV. PAs exert multifactorial effects on norovirus infection, particularly by facilitating virus-induced apoptosis and promoting virion release in MNV-infected cells. Notably, PA depletion using difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), a well-established inhibitor of PA synthesis, effectively suppressed MNV and HNoV infection. Therefore, our results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and highlight the potential of a host-targeting antiviral approach to limit norovirus infection. Furthermore, our findings provide a rationale for further investigating DFMO, a licensed and well-tolerated drug, as a potential therapeutic option for chronic norovirus infections in immunocompromised patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of polyamines in norovirus infection, as therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited due to challenges in cultivating the virus and limited understanding of virus-host interactions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved both murine norovirus (MNV) and human norovirus (HNoV) using human intestinal enteroids as the host model. It was conducted in a laboratory setting with a focus on analyzing the effects of polyamine depletion on viral infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers used functional analysis in MNV-infected cells and human intestinal enteroids to assess the impact of polyamine depletion. They employed difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) to inhibit polyamine synthesis and evaluated viral titers, cytopathic effects, and protein synthesis.
analysis.main_results: Functional analysis showed that polyamine depletion significantly reduced major capsid protein synthesis and viral titers in MNV-infected cells. Similarly, HNoV infection was completely ablated in PA-depleted human intestinal enteroids.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify polyamines as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and suggest that targeting PA metabolism could be a promising antiviral strategy for HNoV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and support the exploration of host-targeting antiviral approaches for limiting norovirus infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on laboratory models and does not include clinical trials. However, the evidence is strong as it directly demonstrates the role of polyamines in both MNV and HNoV infection using well-validated methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of polyamines in norovirus infection, highlighting their critical function in both murine norovirus (MNV) and human norovirus (HNoV). The research demonstrates that polyamine depletion significantly inhibits viral replication and cytopathic effects in MNV-infected cells and completely ablates HNoV infection in human intestinal enteroids. These findings identify polyamines as a novel host dependency factor for norovirus and suggest that targeting polyamine metabolism could offer new therapeutic strategies. The study uses laboratory models and well-established methods to validate its conclusions, providing strong evidence for the potential of host-targeting antiviral approaches. However, the results are based on in vitro systems and do not account for in vivo complexities, which limits their direct application to clinical settings.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of polyamines in norovirus infection, as therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited due to challenges in cultivating the virus and limited understanding of virus-host interactions.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved both murine norovirus (MNV) and human norovirus (HNoV) using human intestinal enteroids as the host model. It was conducted in a laboratory setting with a focus on analyzing the effects of polyamine depletion on viral infection.
elements_en.methods: The researchers used functional analysis in MNV-infected cells and human intestinal enteroids to assess the impact of polyamine depletion. They employed difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) to inhibit polyamine synthesis and evaluated viral titers, cytopathic effects, and protein synthesis.
elements_en.main_results: Functional analysis showed that polyamine depletion significantly reduced major capsid protein synthesis and viral titers in MNV-infected cells. Similarly, HNoV infection was completely ablated in PA-depleted human intestinal enteroids.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify polyamines as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and suggest that targeting PA metabolism could be a promising antiviral strategy for HNoV.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and support the exploration of host-targeting antiviral approaches for limiting norovirus infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on laboratory models and does not include clinical trials. However, the evidence is strong as it directly demonstrates the role of polyamines in both MNV and HNoV infection using well-validated methods.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨多胺在诺如病毒感染中的作用,因为针对诺如病毒感染的治疗策略仍然有限,这主要是由于病毒培养的困难以及对病毒-宿主相互作用的理解不足。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究同时涉及小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)和人类诺如病毒(HNoV),使用人类肠道类器官作为宿主模型。研究在实验室环境中进行,重点分析多胺耗竭对病毒感染的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员在MNV感染的细胞和人类肠道类器官中进行了功能分析,以评估多胺耗竭的影响。他们使用二氟甲基鸟氨酸(DFMO)来抑制多胺合成,并评估了病毒滴度、细胞病变效应和蛋白质合成。
elements_zh.main_results: 功能分析显示,多胺耗竭显著降低了MNV感染细胞中的主要衣壳蛋白合成和病毒滴度。同样,在多胺耗竭的人类肠道类器官中,HNoV感染被完全消除。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现识别出多胺作为新型宿主依赖因子,促进诺如病毒感染,并建议针对多胺代谢的策略可能是HNoV感染的有前景的治疗手段。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为诺如病毒-宿主相互作用提供了新的见解,并支持探索针对宿主的治疗策略以限制诺如病毒感染,特别是在免疫功能低下患者中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于实验室模型,未包括临床试验。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它直接展示了多胺在MNV和HNoV感染中的作用,使用了经过验证的方法。

papers.title_zh: 多胺耗竭抑制小鼠和人类诺如病毒感染
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Noroviruses are non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA viruses in the family Caliciviridae. Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are the leading cause of viral gastrointestinal disease. Despite their clinical relevance, therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited, partly due to challenges in cultivating HNoV and limited understanding of virus-host interactions. Polyamines (PAs) are small polycationic metabolites derived from amino acid metabolism that are essential for diverse cellular functions and serve as important host factors for many RNA viruses. However, their role in norovirus infection has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate that PAs are critical for productive infection for both HNoV and murine norovirus (MNV), underscoring a conserved and functionally significant dependency across species. Functional analysis in MNV-infected cells showed that PA depletion resulted in a marked reduction in major capsid protein synthesis and reduced viral titers following the first replication cycle, coinciding with a loss of virus-induced cytopathic effect (CPE). In PA-depleted cells, viral titers and CPE could be restored by exogenous supplementation with spermine or spermidine (metabolites of the PA biosynthetic pathway), cholesterol, or a PI3-kinase inhibitor. In addition to MNV, depletion of PAs completely ablated HNoV infection in human intestinal enteroids, which was also partially rescued by adding exogenous PAs. Collectively, these findings identify PAs as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and highlight PA metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for antiviral intervention against HNoV. IMPORTANCE: Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide, yet the development of effective antivirals and vaccines has been hampered by the lack of small-animal models and robust in vitro systems to propagate the virus. Murine norovirus (MNV) shares key features with HNoV and serves as a valuable surrogate for studying norovirus biology. In this study, we identify host-derived polyamines (PAs) as essential and conserved metabolites required for productive infection for both HNoV and MNV. PAs exert multifactorial effects on norovirus infection, particularly by facilitating virus-induced apoptosis and promoting virion release in MNV-infected cells. Notably, PA depletion using difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), a well-established inhibitor of PA synthesis, effectively suppressed MNV and HNoV infection. Therefore, our results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and highlight the potential of a host-targeting antiviral approach to limit norovirus infection. Furthermore, our findings provide a rationale for further investigating DFMO, a licensed and well-tolerated drug, as a potential therapeutic option for chronic norovirus infections in immunocompromised patients.
papers.abstract_zh: 未标注:诺如病毒是Caliciviridae科中的无包膜正链RNA病毒。人类诺如病毒(HNoVs)是病毒性胃肠疾病的主要病因。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但针对诺如病毒感染的治疗策略仍然有限,部分原因是HNoV培养的困难以及对病毒-宿主相互作用的理解不足。多胺(PAs)是源自氨基酸代谢的小分子多阳离子代谢物,对多种细胞功能至关重要,并且是许多RNA病毒的重要宿主因子。然而,其在诺如病毒感染中的作用仍不清楚。在这里,我们证明PAs对HNoV和小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)的有产感染至关重要,突显了跨物种的保守且功能重要的依赖性。在MNV感染的细胞中进行的功能分析显示,多胺耗竭导致主要衣壳蛋白合成显著减少,并在第一次复制周期后病毒滴度降低,这与病毒诱导的细胞病变效应(CPE)的丧失同时发生。在多胺耗竭的细胞中,通过外源性补充精胺或精脒(多胺生物合成途径的代谢物)、胆固醇或PI3-激酶抑制剂可以恢复病毒滴度和CPE。除了MNV之外,多胺耗竭完全消除了人类肠道类器官中的HNoV感染,这种效应在添加外源性多胺后部分恢复。这些发现识别出多胺作为新型宿主依赖因子,促进诺如病毒感染,并强调多胺代谢作为针对HNoV感染的潜在治疗靶点。重要性:人类诺如病毒(HNoVs)是全球急性病毒性胃肠炎的主要病因,但由于缺乏小型动物模型和有效的体外系统来传播病毒,开发有效的抗病毒药物和治疗手段受到了阻碍。小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)与HNoV共享关键特征,并可作为研究诺如病毒生物学的有价值的替代模型。在这项研究中,我们确定了源自宿主的多胺(PAs)作为HNoV和MNV有产感染所必需的保守代谢物。多胺对诺如病毒感染具有多方面的影响,特别是在促进病毒诱导的细胞凋亡和促进病毒颗粒释放方面。值得注意的是,使用多胺合成的已知抑制剂二氟甲基鸟氨酸(DFMO)进行多胺耗竭可有效抑制MNV和HNoV感染。因此,我们的结果为诺如病毒-宿主相互作用提供了新的见解,并突出了针对宿主的治疗策略在限制诺如病毒感染方面的潜力。此外,我们的发现为进一步研究DFMO,一种已获许可且耐受性良好的药物,作为免疫功能低下患者慢性诺如病毒感染的潜在治疗选项提供了依据。

papers.title: Human norovirus infection does not induce serotonin secretion in human intestinal organoids
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide. The primary symptoms of HuNoV-associated disease are vomiting and diarrhea; yet the mechanisms underlying these symptoms are poorly understood. Neuroactive hormones such as serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) secreted by intestinal enteroendocrine cells (EECs) can activate vomiting centers in the brain and play a critical role in regulating emetic signaling. Serotonin release from infected EECs has been implicated in vomiting during other enteric infections. Recent studies have reported the detection of HuNoV RNA and antigen in EECs in jejunal biopsies from immunocompromised patients with chronic HuNoV infection and rhesus macaques. We therefore investigated whether HuNoV infection of human intestinal organoids (HIOs) induces serotonin secretion. We examined infection and serotonin secretion with multiple genogroup II HuNoV strains using adult and infant jejunal HIO models, including a doxycycline-inducible neurogenin-3 HIO line with increased numbers of EECs. HuNoV infection did not induce serotonin secretion in either adult or infant HIOs as measured by ELISA. Consistent with enterocytes being the primary target cell type for HuNoVs, GII.4 HuNoV replication was robust in parental HIOs but reduced in EEC-enriched cultures. Furthermore, supernatants from parental HIOs failed to stimulate serotonin release from EEC-enriched HIOs. Together, these findings demonstrate that HuNoV infection of intestinal epithelial cells is insufficient to trigger serotonin release in HIOs. These results suggest that HuNoV-associated vomiting is unlikely to result from direct epithelial serotonin secretion and may require additional cellular components such as immune or neuronal signaling pathways or may involve other neuroactive hormones. IMPORTANCE Vomiting is a hallmark symptom of human norovirus disease. Yet, the biological mechanisms responsible for this response are unknown. Infection of enteroendocrine cells and secretion of serotonin play key roles in the emetic response to other gastrointestinal viruses such as rotavirus. Since recent studies have detected human norovirus antigens and RNA in enteroendocrine cells, we hypothesized that human norovirus infection could stimulate serotonin secretion. We used jejunal human intestinal organoids from adults and infants, including organoids enriched for enteroendocrine cells, and found that infection with several clinically important strains did not induce serotonin secretion, even under conditions supporting robust viral replication. These data indicate that serotonin release from intestinal epithelial cells alone is unlikely to explain norovirus-induced vomiting and highlights the need to investigate alternative mechanisms, including other neuroactive hormones, and neuronal signaling pathways to better understand the pathogenesis of norovirus-associated vomiting.

Serotonin release from infected EECs has been implicated in vomiting during other enteric infections. Recent studies have reported the detection of HuNoV RNA and antigen in EECs in jejunal biopsies from immunocompromised patients with chronic HuNoV infection and rhesus macaques. We therefore investigated whether HuNoV infection of human intestinal organoids (HIOs) induces serotonin secretion. We examined infection and serotonin secretion with multiple genogroup II HuNoV strains using adult and infant jejunal HIO models, including a doxycycline-inducible neurogenin-3 HIO line with increased numbers of EECs. HuNoV infection did not induce serotonin secretion in either adult or infant HIOs as measured by ELISA. Consistent with enterocytes being the primary target cell type for HuNoVs, GII.4 HuNoV replication was robust in parental HIOs but reduced in EEC-enriched cultures. Furthermore, supernatants from parental HIOs failed to stimulate serotonin release from EEC-enriched HIOs. Together, these findings demonstrate that HuNoV infection of intestinal epithelial cells is insufficient to trigger serotonin release in HIOs. These results suggest that HuNoV-associated vomiting is unlikely to result from direct epithelial serotonin secretion and may require additional cellular components such as immune or neuronal signaling pathways or may involve other neuroactive hormones.IMPORTANCEVomiting is a hallmark symptom of human norovirus disease. Yet, the biological mechanisms responsible for this response are unknown. Infection of enteroendocrine cells and secretion of serotonin play key roles in the emetic response to other gastrointestinal viruses such as rotavirus. Since recent studies have detected human norovirus antigens and RNA in enteroendocrine cells, we hypothesized that human norovirus infection could stimulate serotonin secretion. We used jejunal human intestinal organoids from adults and infants, including organoids enriched for enteroendocrine cells, and found that infection with several clinically important strains did not induce serotonin secretion, even under conditions supporting robust viral replication. These data indicate that serotonin release from intestinal epithelial cells alone is unlikely to explain norovirus-induced vomiting and highlights the need to investigate alternative mechanisms, including other neuroactive hormones, and neuronal signaling pathways to better understand the pathogenesis of norovirus-associated vomiting.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 人类诺如病毒(HuNoVs)是全球急性胃肠炎的主要病因之一。HuNoV相关疾病的主要症状是呕吐和腹泻;然而,这些症状的发病机制仍不清楚。肠道内分泌细胞(EECs)分泌的神经活性激素如血清素(5-羟基色胺;5-HT)可以激活大脑中的呕吐中枢,并在调节呕吐信号中起关键作用。在其他肠道感染中,受感染的EECs释放血清素已被认为与呕吐有关。最近的研究报告称,在免疫功能低下且患有慢性HuNoV感染的患者以及恒河猴的空肠活检中检测到了HuNoV RNA和抗原。因此,我们研究了HuNoV感染是否会导致人类肠道类器官(HIOs)中的血清素分泌。我们使用成人和婴儿空肠HIO模型,包括一种四环素诱导的神经元生成素-3 HIO系,该系中EECs数量增加,来检测感染和血清素分泌情况。通过ELISA检测发现,无论是成人还是婴儿HIOs,HuNoV感染均未诱导血清素分泌。这与肠上皮细胞是HuNoV主要靶细胞类型一致,GII.4 HuNoV在亲本HIOs中复制旺盛,但在富含EECs的培养物中复制减少。此外,亲本HIOs的上清液未能刺激富含EECs的HIOs释放血清素。综上所述,这些发现表明HuNoV感染肠道上皮细胞不足以在HIOs中触发血清素释放。这些结果提示HuNoV相关的呕吐不太可能由直接的上皮血清素分泌引起,可能需要其他细胞成分,如免疫或神经信号通路,或者涉及其他神经活性激素。重要性 呕吐是人类诺如病毒疾病的一个标志性症状。然而,导致这种反应的生物学机制尚不清楚。在其他胃肠道病毒如轮状病毒的呕吐反应中,肠道内分泌细胞的感染和血清素的分泌起着关键作用。由于最近的研究在肠道内分泌细胞中检测到了人类诺如病毒抗原和RNA,我们假设人类诺如病毒感染可能刺激血清素分泌。我们使用了成人和婴儿的空肠类器官,包括富含肠道内分泌细胞的类器官,并发现几种临床重要的毒株感染并未诱导血清素分泌,即使在支持病毒高效复制的条件下也是如此。这些数据表明,仅由肠道上皮细胞释放血清素不足以解释诺如病毒引起的呕吐,强调了需要探索其他机制,包括其他神经活性激素和神经信号通路,以更好地理解诺如病毒相关呕吐的发病机制。

analysis_zh.main_results: 无论是成人还是婴儿HIOs,HuNoV感染均未诱导血清素分泌,即使在支持病毒高效复制的条件下也是如此。亲本HIOs的上清液未能刺激富含EECs的HIOs释放血清素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果提示HuNoV相关的呕吐不太可能由直接的上皮血清素分泌引起,可能需要其他细胞成分,如免疫或神经信号通路,或者涉及其他神经活性激素。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究使用HIOs作为模型系统,可能无法完全模拟体内条件,且证据基于体外观察。这些发现的可信度中等。

papers.title: Prolonged Infectivity of Murine Norovirus in Aerosols Suggests Potential for Airborne Transmission.
papers.abstract: Norovirus is a highly contagious enteric virus best known for fecal-oral transmission, but increasing evidence suggests that airborne spread may also contribute to outbreaks. Aerosol transmission of norovirus can occur during episodes involving vomiting, diarrhea, or toilet flushing. To investigate this possibility, the infectivity of aerosolized murine norovirus (MNV) was evaluated over time using influenza A virus (H1N1), a well-established respiratory virus transmitted via aerosols, as a reference control. Aerosols with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 2.38 μm were generated in a 220 L chamber and captured using gelatin filters. MNV infectivity decreased by 2.33 log 10 within the first 3 hours but remained detectable for up to 9 hours, corresponding to a total reduction of 4.2 log 10 . In contrast, H1N1 exhibited a more rapid decay, with a 2.9 log 10 reduction within 3 hours. Overall, these results indicate that MNV retains airborne infectivity for longer durations, supporting the plausibility of aerosol transmission during norovirus outbreak scenarios.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用鼠源性诺如病毒作为模型,这可能无法完全代表人类诺如病毒。由于使用了替代病毒并需要进一步研究以在人类诺如病毒中确认这些发现,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Global resurgence of norovirus GII.17[P17] accompanies shifting phylogeographic connectivity patterns: surveillance in Jiangsu, 2023–2025
papers.abstract: Background Norovirus GII.17[P17] has re-emerged and has been circulating globally since 2023. In Jiangsu, China, we found that its proportion increased from 2024 onward. Using local surveillance data combined with global sequences, we reconstructed the global spatiotemporal dynamics of GII.17[P17] and explored its evolution and molecular mechanisms. Methods Samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing using next-generation sequencing. We used bioinformatics tools to analyze the full viral protein 1 sequences for molecular evolution, spatiotemporal phylogeographic associations, and amino acid changes. Results From October 2024 to May 2025, 209 GII.17[P17] outbreaks were reported (approximately 26 per month), while only 23 outbreaks occurred in the full year of 2023 (fewer than 2 per month). In sporadic case surveillance, the proportion of GII.17[P17] increased from 9.6% in 2023 to 62.4% in January–May 2025. The maximum clade credibility tree showed that GII.17[P17] clustered into two large clusters. Most samples from 2024 to 2025 belonged to Lineage 3 of Cluster II. In the phylogenetic network and minimum spanning tree, we identified three core hub strains. Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns suggest a shift in the primary centers of viral lineage dispersal from East Asia (Cluster I, 2014–2016) to Northwest Europe (Cluster II, 2021–2025). Molecular evolutionary analysis revealed that the current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibited an evolutionary rate of 4.126 × 10 −3 substitutions/site/year (95% HPD: 3.27–4.98 × 10 −3 ), substantially higher than the earlier Cluster I lineages (1.798 × 10 −3 ; 95% HPD: 1.41–2.19 × 10 −3 ; posterior probability >0.99; 95% HPD intervals non-overlapping). Conclusion Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns indicate that the primary centers of GII.17[P17] lineage dispersal have shifted from East Asia (2014–2016) to Northwest Europe (2021–2025). The current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibits an accelerated evolutionary rate, approximately 2.3-fold faster than Cluster I lineages, and carries lineage-specific amino acid substitutions in antigenic epitopes temporally associated with its global expansion. These findings highlight the value of sustained genomic surveillance in regions with high inferred phylogeographic connectivity for monitoring norovirus evolution.

papers.title_zh: 全球诺如病毒 GII.17[P17]病毒再次流行,伴随系统发育地理连接模式的转变:监测在江苏,2023–2025年
papers.source_body_en: Background Norovirus GII.17[P17] has re-emerged and has been circulating globally since 2023. In Jiangsu, China, we found that its proportion increased from 2024 onward. Using local surveillance data combined with global sequences, we reconstructed the global spatiotemporal dynamics of GII.17[P17] and explored its evolution and molecular mechanisms. Methods Samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing using next-generation sequencing. We used bioinformatics tools to analyze the full viral protein 1 sequences for molecular evolution, spatiotemporal phylogeographic associations, and amino acid changes. Results From October 2024 to May 2025, 209 GII.17[P17] outbreaks were reported (approximately 26 per month), while only 23 outbreaks occurred in the full year of 2023 (fewer than 2 per month). In sporadic case surveillance, the proportion of GII.17[P17] increased from 9.6% in 2023 to 62.4% in January–May 2025. The maximum clade credibility tree showed that GII.17[P17] clustered into two large clusters. Most samples from 2024 to 2025 belonged to Lineage 3 of Cluster II. In the phylogenetic network and minimum spanning tree, we identified three core hub strains. Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns suggest a shift in the primary centers of viral lineage dispersal from East Asia (Cluster I, 2014–2016) to Northwest Europe (Cluster II, 2021–2025). Molecular evolutionary analysis revealed that the current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibited an evolutionary rate of 4.126 × 10 −3 substitutions/site/year (95% HPD: 3.27–4.98 × 10 −3 ), substantially higher than the earlier Cluster I lineages (1.798 × 10 −3 ; 95% HPD: 1.41–2.19 × 10 −3 ; posterior probability >0.99; 95% HPD intervals non-overlapping). Conclusion Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns indicate that the primary centers of GII.17[P17] lineage dispersal have shifted from East Asia (2014–2016) to Northwest Europe (2021–2025). The current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibits an accelerated evolutionary rate, approximately 2.3-fold faster than Cluster I lineages, and carries lineage-specific amino acid substitutions in antigenic epitopes temporally associated with its global expansion. These findings highlight the value of sustained genomic surveillance in regions with high inferred phylogeographic connectivity for monitoring norovirus evolution.

papers.title: Systematic functional, genomic, and safety evaluation of food-derived anti-human norovirus candidate Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 is a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae. Here, its in vitro probiotic properties and preliminary safety were evaluated together with whole-genome analysis. The 2.87-Mb genome (46.67% GC; 2757 coding sequences) shared 97.66% average nucleotide identity with L. rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed acid and bile tolerance, retaining approximately 30% survival after 3 h at pH 2.0 and over 40% after 4 h in 0.2% bile salts. During sequential simulated gastrointestinal digestion, L. rhamnosus YQ001 retained 35.98% survival after the gastric phase and 45.06% after the intestinal phase. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed over 90% auto-aggregation at 24 h, while its cell-free supernatant exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities of 85.17% and 76.35%, respectively. Antibacterial activity detected by agar diffusion was abolished after pH neutralization, indicating that the observed inhibition was largely pH-dependent under the tested conditions. L. rhamnosus YQ001 was non-hemolytic and negative for gelatinase and nitroreductase activities. Overall, the phenotypic and genomic findings support the probiotic potential of L. rhamnosus YQ001, while further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is warranted.

The research includes in vitro assessments of acid and bile tolerance, auto-aggregation, and radical-scavenging activities, as well as whole-genome analysis. Results show that the strain retains significant survival under simulated gastrointestinal conditions and exhibits strong antioxidant properties. The authors interpret these findings as supporting the probiotic potential of YQ001 for combating HuNoV, though they emphasize the need for further strain-specific functional and safety evaluations. The study's limitations include reliance on in vitro data and lack of in vivo or clinical testing, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为支持乳酸罗伊氏菌YQ001作为益生菌的潜力,强调其在模拟胃肠道条件下的存活能力和抗氧化特性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,乳酸罗伊氏菌YQ001可能是预防或治疗急性胃肠炎的有前景候选菌株,需要进一步进行针对该菌株的特异性功能和安全性评估。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外评估,未包括临床试验或体内测试,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。由于缺乏直接的人类或动物测试,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001是一种从酸奶中分离的菌株,此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。本研究对其体外益生菌特性及初步安全性进行了评估,并进行了全基因组分析。该菌株的全基因组为2.87 Mb(GC含量46.67%;包含2757个编码序列),与乳酸乳球菌GG ATCC 53103的平均核苷酸同源性为97.66%。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,其无细胞培养上清液表现出85.17%的DPPH自由基清除能力和76.35%的ABTS自由基清除能力。通过琼脂扩散法检测到的抗菌活性在pH中和后被消除,表明在测试条件下观察到的抑制作用主要依赖于pH值。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001不溶血,且不表现出明胶酶和硝基还原酶活性。总体而言,表型和基因组研究结果支持乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为益生菌的潜力,但需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。

papers.title: Evaluation of Human Norovirus Replication in Salivary Gland Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the most common cause of non-bacterial foodborne illnesses worldwide. HuNoVs are notoriously difficult to culture, and current cell culture systems, such as human intestinal enteroids have limitations in efficiency and scalability, which has limited their applications in food safety studies. Recently, it has been shown that transformed salivary gland cell lines (including NS-SV-TT-DC) allow for replication and passaging of norovirus GII.4. Herein, we examined whether we can independently observe viral replication in salivary gland cells and if other strains of human norovirus can replicate in these cells. For this purpose, we first evaluated the replication of several norovirus strains in NS-SV-TT-DC cells by either infecting them with vesicle-cloaked viruses or total viruses in stool filtrates. Low levels of viral replication was observed and vesicle isolation did not improve viral replication. Next, we screened for replication of 50 norovirus samples from 9 genotypes, and 14 isolates demonstrated over a two-fold viral replication. We observed that the initial viral load in the samples does not have a significant effect on replication efficiency. We were also able to successfully passage several isolates. Subsequently, we examined whether interferon inhibitors such as Ruxolitinib, TPCA-1, and BX795 would improve viral replication and observed negligible effects. Finally we tested multiple supplements including MgCl 2 , bile salt, ceramide, and TAK-779. Most supplements had little or no effect on HuNoV replication in NS-SV-TT-DC cells. Bile salt and TAK-779 showed limited, genotype-specific benefits. Altogether these results indicate that salivary gland cells allow limited replication of certain HuNoV isolates. Importance The lack of robust and accessible cell culture systems continues to hinder human norovirus research. Salivary gland cell lines have recently emerged as a promising alternative to human intestinal enteroids because they are easy to maintain and relatively unexpensive. Here, we provide a large-scale independent evaluation of the NS-SV-TT-DC salivary gland model using 50 clinical isolates from multiple human norovirus genotypes. Although several isolates replicated and could be serially passaged, replication was typically modest. Furthermore, multiple approaches commonly used to enhance viral replication in cell culture had little or no effect on system efficiency. These findings establish realistic expectations for the use of this model and provide a framework for future optimization of human norovirus cultivation systems.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 诺如病毒(HuNoVs)是全球范围内非细菌性急性胃肠炎的主要病因。HuNoVs在培养方面极具挑战性,目前的细胞培养系统,如人肠类器官,在效率和可扩展性方面存在局限,这限制了其在食品安全研究中的应用。最近的研究表明,转化的唾液腺细胞系(包括NS-SV-TT-DC)能够支持诺如病毒 GII.4病毒的复制和传代。在此,我们探讨是否可以在唾液腺细胞中独立观察病毒复制,并检查其他人类诺如病毒毒株是否能在这些细胞中复制。为此,我们首先通过感染包被病毒囊或粪便滤液中的总病毒,评估了多种诺如病毒毒株在NS-SV-TT-DC细胞中的复制情况。观察到病毒复制水平较低,且病毒囊的分离并未提高复制效率。随后,我们筛选了来自9种基因型的50个诺如病毒样本,其中14个分离株显示出超过两倍的病毒复制。我们发现样本中的初始病毒载量对复制效率没有显著影响。我们还成功地传代了多个分离株。接着,我们检验了诸如Ruxolitinib、TPCA-1和BX795等干扰素抑制剂是否能提高病毒复制,但观察到效果微乎其微。最后,我们测试了多种补充剂,包括MgCl 2、胆盐、神经酰胺和TAK-779。大多数补充剂对HuNoV在NS-SV-TT-DC细胞中的复制几乎没有影响。胆盐和TAK-779显示出有限的、基因型特异性的益处。综上所述,这些结果表明唾液腺细胞仅能有限地支持某些HuNoV分离株的复制。重要性 缺乏强大且易于获得的细胞培养系统仍然阻碍了人类诺如病毒的研究。由于唾液腺细胞系易于维持且相对成本较低,它们最近成为人肠类器官的有希望替代品。在此,我们使用来自多种人类诺如病毒基因型的50个临床分离株,对NS-SV-TT-DC唾液腺模型进行了大规模独立评估。尽管某些分离株能够复制并进行连续传代,但复制通常较为有限。此外,多种常用于增强细胞培养中病毒复制的方法对系统效率几乎没有影响。这些发现为该模型的使用设定了现实的期望,并为未来优化人类诺如病毒培养系统提供了框架。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估人类诺如病毒(HuNoVs)在唾液腺细胞中的复制,以解决当前HuNoVs细胞培养系统的局限性,这些系统在培养病毒方面存在困难,从而限制了食品安全研究的进展。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用转化的唾液腺细胞系(NS-SV-TT-DC)来评估来自9个基因型的50个诺如病毒样本的复制情况,未提及具体的人类或动物受试者。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员通过感染NS-SV-TT-DC细胞,使用包被囊泡的病毒或粪便滤液中的完整病毒来评估病毒复制;筛选了50个诺如病毒样本的复制情况,并测试了多种补充剂和抑制剂以增强复制。
analysis_zh.main_results: 观察到病毒复制水平较低,且囊泡分离并未提高复制效率。在50个样本中,有14个分离株显示出超过两倍的病毒复制,初始病毒载量对复制效率没有显著影响。某些补充剂和抑制剂显示出有限的、基因型特异性的益处。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究提供了NS-SV-TT-DC模型的大规模评估,表明尽管某些分离株能够复制并进行传代,但复制通常较为有限,且常见的增强复制方法对系统效率几乎没有影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为该模型的使用设定了现实的期望,并为未来优化人类诺如病毒培养系统提供了框架,这可能有助于食品安全研究和相关研究。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括观察到的有限复制以及常见增强复制方法缺乏显著效果,这限制了对模型效用的信心。证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Gut microbiome-enteric virus interactions: mechanisms, clinical implications, and translational directions.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome influences epithelial barrier integrity, metabolite availability, mucosal immune tone, and vaccine responsiveness, all of which are relevant to enterically transmitted viral infection. Norovirus and rotavirus primarily replicate in the intestinal mucosa and cause acute gastroenteritis, whereas poliovirus replicates in the gut and may disseminate systemically. Hepatitis A virus and hepatitis E virus are acquired through the intestine and shed fecally, but their dominant clinical manifestation is hepatitis. This review synthesizes evidence linking the bacteriome, phageome/virome, and mycobiome with these viruses, while explicitly distinguishing direct enteric virus mechanisms from broader microbiome-immune or metabolite pathways and from cross-kingdom evidence extrapolated from intestinal inflammation or pathobiont studies. The strongest evidence supports selected virus-bacterium and virus-metabolite mechanisms, including bacterial glycan interactions in norovirus, bacterial LPS-mediated poliovirus stabilization, bile acid-dependent human norovirus replication in enteroids, and rotavirus-associated barrier disruption. Human studies remain dominated by stool-based associations that are difficult to separate from inflammation, diet, antibiotic exposure, diarrhea, and sampling time. We therefore rank evidence across experimental, organoid, animal, human observational, and clinical-translational levels, and highlight concrete applications for severe gastroenteritis risk prediction, prolonged shedding, impaired barrier recovery, and oral vaccine nonresponse. Future progress will require longitudinal, spatially resolved, multi-kingdom, and multi-omics studies linked to human-relevant experimental systems.

papers.abstract_zh: 肠道微生物组影响上皮屏障完整性、代谢物可用性、粘膜免疫张力和 疫苗 反应性,所有这些都与肠道传播的病毒感染相关。诺如病毒 和轮状病毒主要在肠粘膜中复制并引起 急性胃肠炎,而脊髓灰质炎病毒在肠道中复制并可能全身传播。甲型肝炎病毒和戊型肝炎病毒通过肠道获得并经粪便排出,但其主要临床表现是肝炎。这篇综述综合了细菌组、噬菌体/病毒组和真菌组与这些病毒之间的联系,同时明确区分了直接肠道病毒机制与更广泛的微生物组免疫或代谢途径以及从肠道炎症或致病生物研究中推断出的跨界证据。最有力的证据支持选定的病毒-细菌和病毒-代谢机制,包括 诺如病毒 中的细菌聚糖相互作用、细菌 LPS 介导的脊髓灰质炎病毒稳定性、肠类中胆​​汁酸依赖性人类 诺如病毒 复制以及轮状病毒相关的屏障破坏。人类研究仍然以基于粪便的关联为主,这些关联很难与炎症、饮食、抗生素暴露、腹泻和采样时间分开。因此,我们对实验、类器官、动物、人类观察和临床转化水平的证据进行了排序,并强调了在严重胃肠炎风险预测、长期脱落、屏障恢复受损和口服 疫苗 无反应方面的具体应用。未来的进展将需要与人类相关的实验系统相关的纵向、空间解析、多领域和多组学研究。

papers.title: A Platform Approach to mRNA Purification by Tangential Flow Filtration: Application to a Pentavalent Norovirus Vaccine
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multivalent mRNA vaccines are being evaluated for prevention of norovirus infection caused by multiple circulating strains. Platform purification processes may accelerate development and reduce manufacturing complexity by enabling multiple mRNA constructs to be processed using a common downstream workflow. This study aimed to develop a high-yielding tangential flow filtration (TFF) process for a pentavalent norovirus vaccine comprising five VP1-encoding mRNA constructs from genotypes GI.1, GII.2, GII.3, GII.4 and GII.6. Methods: TFF studies evaluated membrane MWCOs, transmembrane pressures, shear rates, mRNA loadings, and scale-up. Process performance was assessed based on mRNA recovery, integrity, functionality, and apparent hydrodynamic size. Results: Although the VP1 constructs had similar molecular weights (590–610 kDa), initial studies using 100 kDa membranes revealed construct-dependent losses due to permeation of full-length mRNA. Apparent hydrodynamic size was associated with observed membrane sieving behavior, suggesting that transcript-specific structural properties may influence membrane transmission. Reducing the membrane MWCO from 100 to 50 kDa eliminated detectable mRNA permeation while maintaining membrane performance. A shear rate of 4000 s−1 supported higher mRNA loading without compromising recovery or integrity. The resulting 50 kDa process was successfully scaled from 40 cm2 to 1600 cm2 and achieved product yields exceeding 95% across all five VP1 mRNA constructs. Conclusions: These findings support a framework for developing standardized TFF conditions for multivalent mRNA vaccines. The results indicate that transcript molecular weight and nominal membrane MWCO alone may not predict mRNA retention and demonstrate the applicability of a common TFF process across five VP1 mRNA constructs. The proposed influence of RNA conformation on membrane transmission requires confirmation using orthogonal structural methods.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用来自不同基因型的五种 VP1 mRNA 构建体评估了五价 诺如病毒 疫苗 的 TFF 过程。评估该过程的 mRNA 回收率、完整性、功能性和表观流体动力学尺寸。
elements_zh.methods: TFF 研究评估了膜 MWCO、跨膜压力、剪切速率、mRNA 负载和放大。根据 mRNA 回收率、完整性、功能性和表观流体动力学尺寸评估工艺性能。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,将膜 MWCO 从 100 kDa 降低至 50 kDa 可消除可检测到的 mRNA 渗透,同时保持膜性能。4000 s−1 的剪切速率支持更高的 mRNA 负载,而不影响恢复或完整性。由此产生的 50 kDa 过程成功地从 40 cm2 扩展到 1600 cm2,并且在所有五个 VP1 mRNA 构建体中实现了超过 95% 的产物产量。

papers.title: Comparable Norovirus Shedding in Symptomatic and Asymptomatic Individuals: A Hospital-Based Study in Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The frequent detection of norovirus in the stool of healthy people may be due to prolonged norovirus shedding after recovery from illness or asymptomatic infections. We describe norovirus shedding patterns in symptomatic and asymptomatic persons in Bangladesh. Methods We enrolled acute gastroenteritis (AGE) cases and non-AGE controls from two hospitals from January–September, 2023. Fecal samples were tested for norovirus by rapid antigen testing and confirmed by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Positive persons were retested at days 20, 40, 60, and 120 by RT-qPCR. Shedding duration was calculated as the number of days from enrollment to the midpoint between the last norovirus-positive and first norovirus-negative specimens. Cycle threshold (Ct)-values served as an inverse proxy for the viral load. Results Among 16 persons confirmed infected with norovirus (11/32 AGE cases; 5/28 non-AGE controls), a total of 74 stool samples were collected from enrollment through follow-up, of which 28 (38%) were norovirus positive. Of these, 20 (71%) were typed as GII.4 Sydney[P16], 1 as GII.3[P16], and 7 as GII untypeable. The median duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases (10 days, interquartile range [IQR]: 9.5–29 days) and non-AGE controls (9.5 days, IQR: 9.5–49 days). Norovirus Ct-values varied substantially between persons and overlapped significantly among AGE cases and non-AGE controls. Conclusions The quantity and duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases and asymptomatic controls, complicating the attribution of norovirus infection to AGE in Bangladesh. Larger longitudinal studies would more accurately characterize norovirus shedding in resource-limited settings.

papers.title_zh: 有症状和无症状个体的 诺如病毒 脱落情况相当:孟加拉国的一项医院研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background The frequent detection of norovirus in the stool of healthy people may be due to prolonged norovirus shedding after recovery from illness or asymptomatic infections. We describe norovirus shedding patterns in symptomatic and asymptomatic persons in Bangladesh. Methods We enrolled acute gastroenteritis (AGE) cases and non-AGE controls from two hospitals from January–September, 2023. Fecal samples were tested for norovirus by rapid antigen testing and confirmed by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Positive persons were retested at days 20, 40, 60, and 120 by RT-qPCR. Shedding duration was calculated as the number of days from enrollment to the midpoint between the last norovirus-positive and first norovirus-negative specimens. Cycle threshold (Ct)-values served as an inverse proxy for the viral load. Results Among 16 persons confirmed infected with norovirus (11/32 AGE cases; 5/28 non-AGE controls), a total of 74 stool samples were collected from enrollment through follow-up, of which 28 (38%) were norovirus positive. Of these, 20 (71%) were typed as GII.4 Sydney[P16], 1 as GII.3[P16], and 7 as GII untypeable. The median duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases (10 days, interquartile range [IQR]: 9.5–29 days) and non-AGE controls (9.5 days, IQR: 9.5–49 days). Norovirus Ct-values varied substantially between persons and overlapped significantly among AGE cases and non-AGE controls. Conclusions The quantity and duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases and asymptomatic controls, complicating the attribution of norovirus infection to AGE in Bangladesh. Larger longitudinal studies would more accurately characterize norovirus shedding in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Isothermal cross-priming amplification for field-deployable norovirus surveillance: a cost-effective and rapid solution
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Norovirus remains a leading cause of foodborne gastroenteritis globally. While isothermal amplification technologies offer advantages over traditional reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) in terms of speed and portability, there is a lack of domestically developed isothermal amplification systems for norovirus in China. Using a domestic patented cross-priming amplification (CPA) technology, we established CPA systems targeting the predominant norovirus genotypes GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17. The systems were evaluated using 224 fecal samples with confirmed genotypes via sequencing. Our lab-developed CPA (Lab-CPA) systems demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting 98.0% (49/50) of GII.3, 100% (80/80) of GII.4, and 96.9% (31/32) of GII.17 samples, with 100% specificity across all genotypes. Compared to certified clinical RT-qPCR kits, the total percent agreement was 98.7%, 99.3%, and 96.9% for GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17, respectively, accompanied by a significant linear correlation in threshold times. Crucially, the Lab-CPA systems reduced processing time by 44–60 min compared to RT-qPCR. Successful integration into the commercial EasyNAT platform using all-in-one cartridges further streamlined the workflow while maintaining accuracy. Our CPA systems offer a rapid, cost-effective, and streamlined diagnostic solution, ideally suited for point-of-care testing in resource-limited primary healthcare environments. IMPORTANCE Norovirus remains a critical public health threat, driving demand for rapid, deployable diagnostics. While isothermal amplification offers theoretical advantages over reverse transcription quantitative PCR, the absence of domestically developed systems in China has created a reliance on imported assays, limiting point-of-care testing capabilities. This study addresses that gap by establishing a novel cross-priming amplification system tailored to China’s predominant norovirus genotypes. Achieving high sensitivity/specificity and significantly reducing processing time, this work validates a robust, field-adaptable alternative to conventional methods. Furthermore, successful integration with the commercial EasyNAT platform demonstrates immediate translational potential. By providing a cost-effective, high-performance domestic solution, these findings significantly enhance decentralized surveillance and emergency response capacity for norovirus infections in resource-limited settings.

While isothermal amplification technologies offer advantages over traditional reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) in terms of speed and portability, there is a lack of domestically developed isothermal amplification systems for norovirus in China. Using a domestic patented cross-priming amplification (CPA) technology, we established CPA systems targeting the predominant norovirus genotypes GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17. The systems were evaluated using 224 fecal samples with confirmed genotypes via sequencing. Our lab-developed CPA (Lab-CPA) systems demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting 98.0% (49/50) of GII.3, 100% (80/80) of GII.4, and 96.9% (31/32) of GII.17 samples, with 100% specificity across all genotypes. Compared to certified clinical RT-qPCR kits, the total percent agreement was 98.7%, 99.3%, and 96.9% for GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17, respectively, accompanied by a significant linear correlation in threshold times. Crucially, the Lab-CPA systems reduced processing time by 44–60 min compared to RT-qPCR. Successful integration into the commercial EasyNAT platform using all-in-one cartridges further streamlined the workflow while maintaining accuracy. Our CPA systems offer a rapid, cost-effective, and streamlined diagnostic solution, ideally suited for point-of-care testing in resource-limited primary healthcare environments. IMPORTANCE Norovirus remains a critical public health threat, driving demand for rapid, deployable diagnostics. While isothermal amplification offers theoretical advantages over reverse transcription quantitative PCR, the absence of domestically developed systems in China has created a reliance on imported assays, limiting point-of-care testing capabilities. This study addresses that gap by establishing a novel cross-priming amplification system tailored to China’s predominant norovirus genotypes. Achieving high sensitivity/specificity and significantly reducing processing time, this work validates a robust, field-adaptable alternative to conventional methods. Furthermore, successful integration with the commercial EasyNAT platform demonstrates immediate translational potential. By providing a cost-effective, high-performance domestic solution, these findings significantly enhance decentralized surveillance and emergency response capacity for norovirus infections in resource-limited settings.

papers.full_text: Corresponding Author: P. Balaganesan, balaganesanpp@gmail.com Page 1047 RESEARCH PAPER An SEAIHRS–W Norovirus Transmission Model with Asymptomatic Shedding, Hospitalisation, Waning Immunity and An Environmental Reservoir: Analysis Via The Multistage Homotopy Analysis Method D. Adhil Basha1, P. Balaganesan1*, R. Sengothai1, J. Renuka2 1Department of Mathematics, Academy of Maritime Education and Training (AMET) University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India 2Department of Mathematics, Women’s Christian College, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India *Corresponding author. Email address: balaganesanpp@gmail.com (P. Balaganesan) ABSTRACT Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, and its outbreaks in schools are sustained by person-to-person contact and by virus shed into the shared environment. We formulate a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model with asymptomatic infection, hospitalisation, waning immunity and an environmental reservoir. We prove positivity, boundedness and existence of a unique endemic equilibrium when R! > 1, derive R! by the next-generation matrix, and establish global stability of the disease-free equilibrium for R! < 1 and of the endemic equilibrium in the lifelong-immunity limit by Lyapunov functions. The system is solved by the multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM), whose convergence on each stage is proven by a Banach fixed- point argument, with an explicit analyticity radius of at least 0.441 days. Calibrated to the 2001 Derbyshire primary- school outbreak (492 pupils, 201 cases), the model gives R! = 6.21 and an initial effective reproduction number of 3.99, with R" = 0.990 for cumulative cases. Against an RK45 benchmark over 60 days, the third-order MHAM attains a maximum relative error of 1.47 × 10#$% . Sensitivity analysis ranks environmental transmission, virus decay and shedding as dominant, supporting combined hygiene and cleaning interventions. Keywords: Norovirus, Environmental transmission, Multistage homotopy analysis method, Basic reproduction number, Lyapunov stability. Epidemiology and public health burden Norovirus causes an estimated one in five cases of acute gastroenteritis globally and is responsible for a large share of gastroenteritis-related hospitalisations and deaths, particularly among young children and older adults [1]. Most deaths occur in older adults, while the largest number of medically attended cases occurs in young children [1, 3]. The disease is short and usually self-limiting. After a median incubation period of about 1.2 days [4], infected people develop vomiting, diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal cramps that usually resolve within a few days. Treatment is supportive, based on rehydration, and no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral is available [5]. Noroviruses are genetically diverse: they are classified into several genogroups, of which GI, GII and GIV infect humans, and genogroup II accounts for most human infections [5]. This diversity, together with immunity that wanes over several years [6], allows repeated infection throughout life and complicates vaccine design. Transmission routes and outbreak settings Norovirus spreads by the faecal–oral route through direct person-to-person contact, contaminated food and water, and contaminated surfaces. Very few virus particles are needed to cause infection, infected people can shed virus in faeces for weeks, and the virus can remain infectious on surfaces for up to about two weeks [5]. A substantial fraction of infections is asymptomatic. Asymptomatic carriers are less infectious than symptomatic cases, but they shed virus for longer and may therefore sustain transmission between visible outbreaks [7, 6]. These features make semi-closed settings especially vulnerable. Analysis of 7094 outbreaks reported to the US National Outbreak Reporting System during 2009–2017 found a median basic reproduction number of 2.75. Long-term care facilities had the highest setting-specific value, 3.35, and schools, colleges and universities had 2.92 [8]. Transmission was lowest in summer and peaked in autumn and winter [8]. In schools, projectile vomiting in classrooms contaminates shared spaces and exposes many children at once. Bayesian analysis of a 2001 primary-school outbreak in Derbyshire, England, showed that vomiting events were an important route of spread in addition to ordinary person-to-person contact [9]. The same outbreak is used in the present study to calibrate the model. 1.3. Mathematical models of norovirus Mathematical models have been used to estimate transmissibility, the duration of immunity and the effect of control measures. A review by Gaythorpe et al. [7] found published estimates of R! ranging from 1.1 to 7.2. Population-level estimates were generally close to 2, while estimates from individual outbreaks were higher and more variable. The review also noted that most population-level models use SEIR-type structures without explicit environmental compartments, and that asymptomatic infection and waning immunity deserved more attention. Simmons et al. [6] fitted a transmission model with asymptomatic infection to surveillance data from England and Wales and estimated that immunity lasts 4.1–8.7 years. This is far longer than the months suggested by early challenge studies. The environmental route has been examined explicitly in a smaller number of studies. Towers et al. [10] fitted a model with direct and environmental transmission to daily incidence from a cruise-ship outbreak. They estimated a combined reproduction number of 1.6 and found that direct transmission between passengers predominated in that setting. Wang et al. [11] fitted a model with two transmission routes to 23 school outbreaks in Jiangsu Province, China. They estimated mean effective reproduction numbers of 8.92 for person-to-person spread and 2.19 for water- or food-borne spread, and showed that isolating symptomatic cases sharply reduces peak incidence. A second line of work has focused on mathematical structure and numerical schemes. Raezah et al. [12] formulated a fractional-order model with vaccination and asymptomatic carriers under the Atangana– Baleanu–Caputo operator and solved it with an Adams–Bashforth scheme based on Newton polynomials. Cui et al. [13] combined a fractal– fractional operator with stochastic perturbations in a model with vaccination. Song et al. [14] studied a stochastic model driven by Lévy noise in which water and food contamination are explicit compartments. Ahmad et al. [15] analysed a fractional model with transmission through contaminated food and water. Saleem et al. [2] analysed a fractional SEIR model with a Grünwald– Letnikov nonstandard finite-difference scheme. Alqudah et al. [16] studied a discrete fractional SEAIRF model with an environmental reservoir and used a neural network to predict its dynamics. Several recent studies have combined analysis with control. Ndendya et al. [17] modelled vaccination, treatment and public-health education, computed the reproduction number by a graph-theoretic method and estimated parameters from US outbreak surveillance data for 2023–2024. Gogovi et al. [5] included environmental reservoirs, waning immunity and reinfection, proved global stability by Lyapunov functions and solved an optimal control problem. They found that the environmental transmission and shedding rates dominate the reproduction number and that hand hygiene is the most effective single intervention. 1.4. Semi-analytical solution methods Most of the studies above rely on numerical schemes, which give accurate trajectories but no explicit expression for the solution. Semi-analytical series methods instead produce closed-form approximations that show how each parameter enters the local dynamics and that can be differentiated directly. The homotopy analysis method (HAM) of Liao [18] constructs a continuous deformation from an initial guess to the exact solution. It contains an auxiliary convergence-control parameter ħ that can be used to enlarge the region of convergence. With a suitable choice of ħ, HAM reduces to the homotopy perturbation method and to the Adomian decomposition method. The Laplace–Adomian decomposition method has been applied to several epidemic models, including Lassa fever and malaria [20, 21]. A known weakness of all single-interval series methods is that a truncated series is accurate only near its expansion point. Epidemic curves evolve over weeks, so a single series is usually inadequate over the whole outbreak. The multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM) restarts the series on short successive intervals and so extends the solution over long horizons. Its practical value, however, depends on knowing how long each interval may be before the series stops converging. Existing applications usually choose the step length by trial and error and verify convergence only numerically. 1.5. Research gap and contributions To our knowledge, no published norovirus model combines (i) asymptomatic infection with reduced infectiousness, (ii) hospitalisation with disease- induced death, (iii) waning immunity and (iv) an environmental reservoir, together with a semi- analytical solution whose convergence is proven rather than assumed. In addition, few norovirus models that include an environmental compartment have been calibrated to case data from a documented outbreak. This paper addresses these gaps. Its main contributions are as follows. 1. We formulate a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model and prove positivity, boundedness and existence of a positively invariant region. 2. We derive R! by the next-generation matrix and decompose it into direct and environmental contributions from asymptomatic and symptomatic carriers. We also obtain the endemic equilibrium explicitly. 3. We prove global stability of the disease-free equilibrium for R! < 1 by a Lyapunov function. For the endemic equilibrium we prove global stability only in the lifelong- immunity limit (ω= 0), by a Volterra-type Lyapunov function; with waning immunity (ω> 0) we establish local stability for the calibrated parameters. 4. We derive explicit MHAM solutions from zeroth to third order for every compartment. We prove convergence on each stage by a Banach fixed-point argument that yields a computable bound on the stage length. 5. We calibrate the model to the Derbyshire 2001 school outbreak, quantify uncertainty by parametric bootstrap, examine identifiability of the transmission routes and of the assumed environmental decay, test out-of-sample prediction, and validate the MHAM solution against an RK45 benchmark. 6. We quantify the sensitivity of R! , of the peak size and timing and of cumulative cases by Latin hypercube sampling with partial rank correlation, and evaluate combined hygiene and cleaning interventions. 1.6. Section 6 describes the data, calibration and numerical methods, and Section 7 reports the results. Sections 8–10 discuss the findings, limitations and public health significance, and Section 11 concludes. 2. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop and analyze a mathematical model to understand the transmission dynamics of norovirus, particularly focusing on its role in outbreaks in schools. Norovirus is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis, and its persistence in the environment contributes to sustained outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model calibrated to a 2001 Derbyshire primary-school outbreak involving 492 pupils and 201 cases. The model incorporates asymptomatic shedding, hospitalisation, waning immunity, and an environmental reservoir.
analysis.methods: The model was solved using the multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM), with convergence proven via a Banach fixed-point argument. Sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify key parameters influencing transmission, including environmental spread, virus decay, and shedding rates.
analysis.main_results: The model yielded a basic reproduction number (R0) of 6.21 and an initial effective reproduction number of 3.99. The cumulative effective reproduction number (R") was found to be 0.990. The MHAM demonstrated a maximum relative error of 1.47 × 10$-4$ compared to an RK45 benchmark over 60 days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the results as highlighting the importance of environmental transmission in norovirus outbreaks. The novelty lies in the formulation of a comprehensive model that accounts for asymptomatic shedding, waning immunity, and environmental reservoirs, providing insights into control strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the implementation of combined hygiene and cleaning interventions to mitigate norovirus transmission, particularly in school settings where outbreaks are common. They also offer a framework for modeling and predicting the spread of norovirus in human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mathematical model and does not include empirical data from real-world outbreaks. The evidence strength is moderate, as the model is based on calibrated data and theoretical analysis, but lacks direct observational validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model to analyze norovirus transmission dynamics, incorporating asymptomatic shedding, hospitalisation, waning immunity, and an environmental reservoir. The model is calibrated to a 2001 Derbyshire primary-school outbreak, yielding a basic reproduction number (R0) of 6.21 and an initial effective reproduction number of 3.99. The model's solution, using the multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM), demonstrates a maximum relative error of 1.47 × 10$-4$ over 60 days. Sensitivity analysis identifies environmental transmission, virus decay, and shedding as dominant factors, supporting combined hygiene and cleaning interventions. The study's findings offer insights into norovirus control strategies in school environments but are limited to theoretical modeling without direct observational validation, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

They also offer a framework for modeling and predicting the spread of norovirus in human populations.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mathematical model and does not include empirical data from real-world outbreaks. The evidence strength is moderate, as the model is based on calibrated data and theoretical analysis, but lacks direct observational validation.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop and analyze a mathematical model to understand the transmission dynamics of norovirus, particularly focusing on its role in outbreaks in schools. Norovirus is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis, and its persistence in the environment contributes to sustained outbreaks.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study employed a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model calibrated to a 2001 Derbyshire primary-school outbreak involving 492 pupils and 201 cases. The model incorporates asymptomatic shedding, hospitalisation, waning immunity, and an environmental reservoir.
analysis_en.methods: The model was solved using the multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM), with convergence proven via a Banach fixed-point argument. Sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify key parameters influencing transmission, including environmental spread, virus decay, and shedding rates.
analysis_en.main_results: The model yielded a basic reproduction number (R0) of 6.21 and an initial effective reproduction number of 3.99. The cumulative effective reproduction number (R") was found to be 0.990. The MHAM demonstrated a maximum relative error of 1.47 × 10$-4$ compared to an RK45 benchmark over 60 days.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the results as highlighting the importance of environmental transmission in norovirus outbreaks. The novelty lies in the formulation of a comprehensive model that accounts for asymptomatic shedding, waning immunity, and environmental reservoirs, providing insights into control strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the implementation of combined hygiene and cleaning interventions to mitigate norovirus transmission, particularly in school settings where outbreaks are common. They also offer a framework for modeling and predicting the spread of norovirus in human populations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mathematical model and does not include empirical data from real-world outbreaks. The evidence strength is moderate, as the model is based on calibrated data and theoretical analysis, but lacks direct observational validation.

papers.full_text: AbstractBackgroundAcute gastroenteritis causes morbidity across all age groups, and timely, effective identification of its etiologic agents is essential for clinical management and antimicrobial stewardship. Conventional diagnostic methods have limited sensitivity and often fail to detect coinfections or specific bacterial pathotypes. In contrast, molecular methods, such as FilmArray panels, are rapid, highly sensitive, and capable of detecting coinfections. This study aimed to characterize gastrointestinal pathogens detected by the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BioFire Diagnostics, LLC, Salt Lake City, UT, USA; a bioMérieux company) and to evaluate their association with demographic and clinical characteristics among patients at Hospital Angeles Lindavista, Mexico City, Mexico.MethodsA retrospective observational study conducted from January 2022 to July 2025 included all patients who underwent gastrointestinal molecular testing. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and multiplex PCR results were extracted from electronic medical records and the FilmArray database. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, logistic regression, Fisher’s exact test, and Spearman correlation.ResultsAn analysis of 1,120 samples found an overall positivity rate of 906 (81%). Coinfections were present in 543 (49%) cases. The most common pathogens were enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (E. coli, EPEC; 374, 33.4%); enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC; 281, 25.1%); and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC; 231, 20.6%). Rotavirus A (206, 18.4%) and norovirus GI/GII (168, 15%) were the most frequent. Positivity was highest in children under five (147, 84.48%) and lowest in adults over 60 (129, 73.71%). Seasonal patterns showed unexpected peaks of rotavirus in spring-summer and of Cyclospora cayetanensis in summer. No significant association was found between pathogen presence and comorbidities, likely due to many missing clinical details. A negative correlation among major E. coli pathotypes suggests competitive exclusion.ConclusionThe BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel identified pathogen patterns that conventional methods miss. Age and seasonal trends highlight the need for localized epidemiological surveillance. These results encourage the use of molecular diagnostics in routine assessments of gastrointestinal infections and support antimicrobial stewardship efforts. Future studies should include clinical severity metrics and evaluate patient outcomes to connect molecular detection with clinical significance.Keywords: acute gastroenteritis, antimicrobial stewardship, e. coli pathotypes, gastrointestinal pathogens, molecular diagnostics, seasonal trends Materials and methodsStudy designWe conducted a retrospective, observational, cross-sectional study at Hospital Angeles Lindavista from January 2022 to July 2025. Its goal was to identify and examine gastrointestinal pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and parasites, detected by the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BioFire Diagnostics, LLC, Salt Lake City, UT, USA; a bioMérieux company). The study aimed not only to understand epidemiological patterns but also to associate these pathogens with patients' demographic and clinical features; it included all patients who received a gastrointestinal molecular panel, whether as outpatients or while hospitalized. Analyzed variables included demographics, patient type, comorbidities, risk factors, diagnoses, detected pathogens, and infection type. Data sources included the FilmArray multiplex PCR system database (by bioMérieux) and the Hospital Angeles Lindavista Electronic Clinical History (ECH) database.Laboratory testingSamples examined were stool specimens. We identified gastrointestinal pathogens using the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel multiplex PCR system. This certified device combines nucleic acid extraction, reverse transcription, first-stage multiplex PCR, and second-stage nested PCR within a single disposable pouch. It employs freeze-dried reagents and multiple primers optimized for a common annealing temperature, allowing simultaneous qualitative detection of 22 gastrointestinal pathogens, such as diarrheagenic E. coli types, Campylobacter, Salmonella, Vibrio, Yersinia enterocolitica, Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile) toxin A/B, Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia, adenovirus F40/41, astrovirus, norovirus GI/GII, rotavirus A, and sapovirus. All steps occur inside sealed blister compartments in the pouch, reducing manual handling and contamination risk and delivering results in about an hour. We performed tests following the manufacturer's protocols. Results labeled "detected" or "not detected" were considered valid. If a process failed, we marked the result "invalid" and repeated the test. This approach improves diagnostic speed and helps detect coinfections but has limitations: sensitivity varies among targets; it does not quantify microbial load, so it cannot differentiate active infection from colonization or residual nucleic acids, and it detects only organisms within the panel and cannot identify pathogens outside it. A negative result does not rule out microorganisms not among the panel's targets. Therefore, we interpreted results alongside clinical presentation and additional diagnostics.Data sourceWe compiled a retrospective database from Hospital Angeles Lindavista for the specified period, including data from 1,120 patients. We de-identified the patients' data and standardized and grouped variable coding for analysis.Statistical analysisStatistical analyses were conducted using R version 4.5.1 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria) in RStudio (Posit Software, PBC, Boston, MA, USA).Descriptive AnalysisCategorical variables were summarized with their absolute counts and percentages. For the continuous variable (age), we assessed the data distribution and reported the mean and standard deviation (SD). Overall and age-specific positivity rates were calculated by dividing detected cases by the total samples processed.Seasonality AnalysisWe examined the monthly detection frequency of the top 10 most common pathogens over the study period (2022-2025) to identify seasonal trends and periodic fluctuations.Inferential Analysis and AssociationsTo analyze links between clinical variables (such as comorbidities and risk factors) and pathogen presence, we used binary logistic regression to calculate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For small subgroups (n < 5), we used Fisher's exact test for sensitivity checks.Finally, to investigate microbial interactions (coinfections versus mutual exclusion), we created a correlation matrix based on Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, considering only statistically significant interactions.All statistical tests used a significance threshold of p < 0.05 (two-tailed).Ethical considerationsThe Research Ethics Committee of Hospital Angeles Pedregal approved the study protocol (approval number: HAP 2786). All procedures followed the ethical standards outlined in the Declaration of Helsinki. The committee granted a waiver of informed consent for this retrospective study because of its minimal-risk design. Confidentiality and data protection were maintained throughout the study. ResultsCharacteristics of the study populationA total of 1,120 samples from patients with suspected gastrointestinal infection treated at Hospital Angeles Lindavista between January 2022 and July 2025 were analyzed. The mean age of the patients was 33.6 years (SD ± 23.1). A balanced gender distribution was observed, with 616 (55%) female patients. Most samples (1,028, 92%) were from hospitalized patients, while 92 (8%) were from outpatients (Table 1).Table 1Clinical and demographic characteristics of the study population.For the age variable, the values correspond to the mean and standard deviation (SD).
